questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Somewhere in europe, not too expensive, close to boarders and a big city with a lot of opportunities. i wanted to experience a lot while being abroad but not having to break my bank account. Also having a lot of fun with other students from other countries

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had so much fun i just had some trouble with one teacher that caused me distress

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: quite easy they always update you with emails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: introduction days and a lot of social activities from the get go

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
it was really hard i used WG and wrote in german and still i only got 1 offer which luckily got. 
the school also offer dorms and there are other apps/websites but i don't really remember the names of them - facebook is NOT an option

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Depends on the area you live in but its always very smart to live close to a station of some sort to get around easier.
I loved living off campus

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: i didn't live there but the school offered me a dorm. the dorms are quite far away from the citycenter so that's a disadvantage but they are really cheap. I didn't like how dirty it looked, maybe its regular dorm standards but i was happy to share an apartment with 2 others and not 10 others

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: the registration is complicated because KU has a lot of deadlines but the semester in Germany is odd compared to here which means you don't know which courses are available when you have to provide it in the OLA. Be patient and just choose something ahah most of the courses will happen (maybe the name of the course will change but typically not the content)

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: difficult but so is it for every uni. I think maybe this one is one of the easier registrations, i only had issues regarding uploading the health insurance card (blue card) but other than that it was okay

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: coordinators from the host uni will provide a step by step guide of how to register

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: very i got every class except the german class i wanted in the beginning but managed to get a spot later on so no issues with classes

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: just be prepared to spend a lot of time

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: very interesting courses

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: mostly MA i only took 1 BA course, BA courses are usually in german

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: its very old school, test on paper, very short exams 1-1,5 hours. very much know-it-all-by-heart exams. but no books so everything is based on the slides presented at lectures so preparation before class is usually not necessary

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: German A1.2+A2.1, introduction to bioinformatics, darkside of mikrobiology (microbiologi as a warfare agent), hot topics in infectious diseases, starter cultures lab, parasitic immunology, english introduction to academic writing

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
they where all really interesting, some harder than others but overall easy 
but the teacher from bioinformatics is not that nice - the course is in german and not english even though the website state its in english so just don't choose that if you don't have to

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: there is a radio cost in most housings not in mine so i didn't get charged but usually its mandatory

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
transportation, deutschland ticket including busses, trams, u-bahns and s-bahns and regional trains for the whole country and some parts of austria only 300 kr pr month!?
food, beer, drinks and coffee is also less expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
sportsclub for everything very cheap on every campus! super nice, a lot of students clubs as well and many events hosted by students for students 
! very very nice

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: literally everything, pilates, soccer, tennis, volley, gym, dance, crossfire, bachata, food clubs, movie clubs. everything

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
ESN are hosting a lot of different events always, helps in the introduction days, host movie/dance/food/kareoke nights, language cafes, hiking clubs  and weekendtrips
so nice when you don't know what to do,

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: HIKE

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
no speak german ahaha
i mostly hung out with other exchange students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: not really any

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: casual beer drinking, and hiking - never hiked before coming and didn't even have the right clothing for it but made it work and the scenery is beautiful

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: be prepared to hike, go to cute coffee shops and drink beer!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
such a cute place
both munich and freising (where my campus is) are beautiful! munich is a perfect student city and trains connect the city very well to hiking opportunities and other beautiful cities even in other countries, we went to prag, bologna, milan, venice, and salzburg! we also went to closer destinations to explore a bit

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: meeting lovely people

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: i don't know i had fun

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: GO TO MUNICH

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
